solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fish, small one that sleeps

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
someone who takes a nap, a short sleep

explanation.surface: A sleepy little fish dozing on the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits definition from wordplay: the fish comes first, then a short charade of size and sleeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapper is a family of warm-water food fish with sharp teeth, common on restaurant menus.

clue.text: Season piece of wood as a good place to start

parts.note: one of the four seasons of the year
a flat plank of timber

explanation.surface: Advice on seasoning timber before using it to begin a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' reads as a verb, as in seasoning wood, but it is the noun for a time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a springboard is anything that launches you into action, just as the diving board launches a diver.

clue.text: Who might check movement of cash coming from Saudi to Russia

definitions.text: Who might check movement of cash

indicators.note: what comes from inside a phrase is drawn out of its run of letters, so the result sits within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the word boundaries of this phrase

explanation.surface: Someone monitoring money being transferred from Saudi Arabia to Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside sAUDI TO Russia; the international money-laundering picture distracts from the plain run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is an accountant who examines financial records to verify where money has gone.

clue.text: Reach up at drifting item slowly moving earthwards

indicators.note: drifting things wander out of place, so these letters move into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, taken as written

explanation.surface: Stretching upward to catch something floating gently down from the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drifting' fits the descending object so well that it hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A parachute is a canopy that slows a falling person or cargo so it descends gently to the ground.

clue.text: Take exception to gift papa has left

indicators.note: something that has left is no longer there, so a letter departs from the word

parts.note: a present is a gift
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone offended by a present after their father walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESENT loses its P to leave RESENT; Papa is the radio code word for the letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter or aggrieved about it, which is to object or be offended.

clue.text: A party's sent back drink

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party, with the possessive adding S

explanation.surface: A drink returned to the bar by someone at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is informal British for a party or celebration; the apostrophe S is read as a plain letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is fizzy water or a carbonated soft drink, often used as a mixer.

clue.text: Health resort in Spain, not at home

indicators.note: saying not excludes something, so those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: the country, taken as written
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A Spanish health resort to visit while you are away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAIN without IN leaves the resort; 'at home' giving IN is a staple crossword equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a town or resort with mineral springs, visited for health treatments and relaxation.

clue.text: Leading editor set up magazine, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: being at the top is leading
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A senior editor launching a new magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The publishing picture makes 'magazine' a periodical, but here it is an arms store; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine in the military sense is a storehouse for ammunition, one kind of depot or storage site.

clue.text: Equestrian in condition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person on horseback
second meaning: an extra clause added to a document

explanation.surface: A horseman in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In condition' reads as fit and healthy, but 'in' just joins two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is both a horseman and an added stipulation or proviso attached to an agreement or bill.

clue.text: Go away, packing some current hair product

indicators.note: packing means stuffing something inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: shoo is what you say to send someone away
an amp is a unit of electrical current

explanation.surface: Telling someone to leave as they pack up some fashionable hair care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests up-to-date, but it is electrical current, measured in amps.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is the liquid soap used for washing hair, a basic toiletry.

clue.text: Organisation's instructions about actor's part

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: orders are instructions
an actor's part is made up of lines, with the possessive adding S

explanation.surface: A theatre company's directions concerning an actor's role.
explanation.walkthrough: Both apostrophe S endings work: on 'Organisation' it stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; on 'actor' it is a letter of the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderliness is the state of being neat and well arranged, which is good organisation.

clue.text: Enthusiast for fruit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal word for a fanatic or devotee
second meaning: a hard-shelled seed, botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone who is crazy about fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enthusiast for fruit' reads as a fruit lover, but 'for' only links two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a fanatic is called a nut, as in a fitness nut, and botanically a nut is a dry fruit.

clue.text: On one occasion having interrupted, referred to as egocentric

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so one piece has broken into the middle of another

parts.note: to cite is to refer to
once means on one occasion

explanation.surface: Someone who once butted in and got called self-absorbed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: ONCE breaks into CITED; the conversational picture hides that 'referred to' is a single verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited person has an excessively high opinion of themselves, being vain and self-centred.

clue.text: Fair, quite flexible and competent

indicators.note: flexible things bend into new shapes, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
able means capable or competent

explanation.surface: A testimonial describing someone as reasonable, adaptable and capable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flexible' looks like one in a list of virtues, but it signals the rearrangement of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable means just and impartial, treating everyone evenly, which is a synonym of fair.

clue.text: Ship richly ornamented, but not old

indicators.note: saying but not excludes something, so a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: baroque describes an elaborately decorated style
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A vessel with lavish decoration that is nonetheless brand new.
explanation.walkthrough: BAROQUE minus its O gives the sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a sailing vessel with three or more masts, square-rigged except for the rear mast.

clue.text: Grumble millions express

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
to utter is to express in words

explanation.surface: Huge numbers of people voicing their complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' might be a fast train or an adjective, but here it is the verb for saying something.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutter is to complain in a low, indistinct voice, a near synonym of grumbling.

clue.text: Earth goes beyond fossil fuel

parts.note: to top something is to exceed it
oil is a fossil fuel

explanation.surface: The planet's future depends on moving past fossil fuels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth' reads as the planet in this climate picture, but it is the soil in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsoil is the fertile upper layer of soil, and earth in the gardening sense means soil.

clue.text: Consent to what one might do with unruly hair?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to allow or authorise

definitions.text: what one might do with unruly hair?
definitions.note: a cryptic phrase read as two words
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read whimsically: give the hair a permanent wave

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a hairdresser taming wild hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits as PERM IT; a perm is a chemical treatment that sets hair in curls or waves.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to allow, the same as giving consent to something happening.

clue.text: Mum's eaten stewed game?

indicators.note: stewing a dish churns and breaks down its contents, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, with the possessive S included

explanation.surface: Mother has had some game casserole, such as venison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like wild meat in a stew; the question mark warns that it is a pastime, one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A game is a form of entertainment or pastime, one example of an amusement.

clue.text: Relative confused when missing a run

indicators.note: what is missing is absent, so those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: unclear means muddled or confused
taken as written
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A family member bewildered after missing a run in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCLEAR drops A and R, the letters for 'a run'.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is the brother of a parent, so he is a family relative.

clue.text: Quietly greeting character in Mykonos

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical marking for quiet
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: Softly saying hello to someone on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person met on holiday, but it is a letter; Mykonos is a Greek island, pointing to the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet, a written symbol used on Mykonos.

clue.text: Ring in the month for Christmas spirit and decency

indicators.note: in places one thing within another, so a piece sits inside the rest

parts.note: DEC is the abbreviation for December
the letter O is ring-shaped
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Welcoming December with festive cheer and good behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas spirit' reads as festive goodwill, but the words split: the month is December and the spirit is rum, with O set between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, dignified behaviour, essentially a synonym of decency and propriety.

clue.text: Crash into wreck being raised

indicators.note: in a down entry, something raised is lifted so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or wreck

explanation.surface: A collision with a sunken wreck as it is hauled up from the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' looks like a noun for a sunken ship, but it is the verb meaning to spoil.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram something is to strike it forcefully, the same as crashing into it.

clue.text: Share dealer, almost penniless

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short

parts.note: a stockbroker deals in shares

explanation.surface: A stockbroker who has nearly run out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: BROKER loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being broke is the informal way of saying you have no money at all.

clue.text: Ray is a fish out of river

indicators.note: out of here means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: the bream is a freshwater fish
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A ray is a kind of fish stranded out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like the flat fish, which seems confirmed by the rest; it is actually a ray of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam is a shaft of light, a synonym of ray as in a ray of sunshine.

clue.text: What supports heads of trailing roses everywhere like lilacs in spring

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only the opening letter of each is kept

parts.words: trailing roses everywhere like lilacs in spring
parts.note: the opening letter of each of these seven words

explanation.surface: Describing the garden frame that holds up climbing roses and spring lilacs.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a garden frame holding up climbing flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework of wood or wire that supports climbing plants in a garden.
